At Olympian Way, adjustments in the intersection were made to eliminate a jog, thus providing a smoother transition in north-south vehicle travel.
Another location shift occurs at the intersection of Lincoln Highway and Indiana Street where presently Indiana Street, Olympic Circle and Kedzie Street all intersect Lincoln Highway within a distance of 200 feet. This intersection was relocated as a four-way right-angled intersection to facilitate traffic safety.
At Western Avenue, the proposed improvement merges the six-lane cross-section into a four-lane section which then follows the existing centerline of Lincoln High-way to Edgewood Avenue where the cross-section narrows from two 24-foot lanes to two 22-foot lanes to adjust to the cross-section of the western end of the improvement at Lincoln Highway and Chicago Road. Through this section, from Western Avenue to Edgewood Avenue, the built-up urban nature of the area precludes moving the location off the existing centerline of Lincoln Highway.
2. Alignment B
Alignment B investigates the potential of shifting the new road centerline to either side to place the additional right-of-way takings entirely to one side. For the portion of the route west of Western Avenue the preferred combination of these shifts to north or south of the present centerline was used. East of Western Avenue through the heavily developed areas the alignment is identical to that used for Alignment A. Right-of-way takings in this area are minimized by placing the new centerline on the existing centerline.
From Cicero Avenue eastward to Kildare Avenue the new centerline is moved to the north of the existing centerline. Although the area is lightly developed, fewer improvements are effected by taking all new right-of-way on the north.
